summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with stage IV cholangiocarcinoma and a history of biliary stents and recurrent infections, was admitted with fever, chills, and lack of output from his percutaneous biliary drain, consistent with cholangitis and early sepsis. On admission, he underwent percutaneous balloon dilation and exchange of his biliary drain. Blood cultures grew E. coli, prompting a switch to IV meropenem. An MRCP showed signs of cholangitis and biliary stenosis, leading to an ERCP for clearance of sludge and debris from the stents. His biliary drain was subsequently capped, and he improved clinically with normalized liver enzymes and resolution of fever. He was diagnosed with bacteremia and newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes, managed with insulin and diet. He was discharged home with a plan for 10 days of IV meropenem via home health, prophylactic oral vancomycin, and follow-up for liver tests and oncology care.
